game.title: Aethermoor
game.subtitle: Chronicles of Another World
pack.base.name: Aethermoor base content
dlg.mira.offer: Welcome, adventurer! Slimes are overrunning the plains. Could you lend a hand?
dlg.mira.accepted: Great! Defeat five of them and come back to me.
dlg.mira.busy: The slimes are still out there. Come back once you have beaten five.
dlg.mira.thanks: Excellent work! Here is your reward.
dlg.mira.cellar_offer: One more thing. Under the old mill at Mossveil, north-east of here, a Gel King has been feeding on every slime for miles. Will you drain that cellar?
dlg.mira.cellar_accepted: Good. It is wet and crowded in there, and the King is slow but heavy. Wake the stone at the door first.
dlg.mira.cellar_busy: The Gel King is still down in the cellar. Mind the slimes around him.
dlg.mira.cellar_thanks: The Mossveil cellar is quiet and the plains are safe again. You are a real adventurer now.
dlg.mira.barrow_offer: There is something worse than slimes. Grunmoor Barrow, to the north-west, has woken up: a Warden walks its halls. Will you put it to rest?
dlg.mira.barrow_accept: I will go to the barrow.
dlg.mira.barrow_accepted: Be careful. Wolves and blue slimes nest inside, and the Warden hits hard. There is a Threshold Stone at the door; use it to heal.
dlg.mira.barrow_busy: The Warden is still in the barrow. Take a potion and go back.
dlg.mira.barrow_thanks: The barrow is quiet again, and it is thanks to you. The guild will remember.
ui.stone_awake: The stone awakens and hums. You feel restored.
ui.stone_rest: The stone hums. You feel restored.
ui.journal_empty: No quests yet. Talk to people and visit the guild.

dlg.mira.mine_offer: Word came from the guild hall of Ironspine, far to the north-east beyond the mountains. The old mine is sealed: an iron foreman that no one hired keeps working it. It is a long road. Will you go?
dlg.mira.mine_accepted: Pack bread and potions, and wake the Threshold Stones of the towns you pass: they will bring you home. The mine has a stone at its door too.
dlg.mira.mine_busy: The foreman is still hammering in the Ironspine mine. Take your time on the road, but come back alive.
dlg.mira.mine_thanks: The hammering has stopped in Ironspine. The guild owes you more than I can pay, but I will keep trying.
dlg.mira.temple_offer: The coast folk of Tidehaven, far to the south-west, say a drowned temple has risen from the bay at low tide, and a Regent in it drowns anyone who passes. Will you cross the land to them?
dlg.mira.temple_accepted: Take a boat of patience, not just a sword. The temple has a Threshold Stone at its steps; wake it before you go in.
dlg.mira.temple_busy: The Regent still sits in the Drowned Temple. The tide will not wait forever, so do not rush in.
dlg.mira.temple_thanks: The bay is calm again and the fishers sing your name. I will tell the guild.
dlg.mira.cavern_offer: The last letter is the worst. In the far north a cavern under the Frostveil glaciers breathes cold, and a Revenant in it freezes whole caravans. It is the longest road of all. Will you go?
dlg.mira.cavern_accepted: Dress warm and carry potions. The cavern has a Threshold Stone at its mouth. Come back with the cold gone from your bones.
dlg.mira.cavern_busy: The Revenant is still in the cavern, and the north is still cold. Come back alive.
dlg.mira.cavern_thanks: Frostveil is quiet. Rest a moment, because there is one more letter on my desk, and then another.
dlg.mira.hollow_offer: A tracker came in from the Whisperwood, white as milk. Far to the north-west there is a hollow in the forest where the trees stand in a ring, and something silver-black runs the shade wolves like a pack-mother. Hunters no longer go in. Will you?
dlg.mira.hollow_accept: I will go to the Whisperwood.
dlg.mira.hollow_accepted: Walk quietly and light a lamp at dusk. The hollow has a Threshold Stone at its mouth, just outside the ring of trees.
dlg.mira.hollow_busy: The Alpha still keeps the hollow. The forest is listening, so do not hurry.
dlg.mira.hollow_thanks: The tracker sleeps through the night now. The Whisperwood is only a forest again.
dlg.mira.ziggurat_offer: Far to the south-east the dunes of Sunscar have given up a ziggurat that the sand had swallowed. A Sentinel walks its rings, and the caravans have stopped passing near. It is a long way under the sun. Will you go?
dlg.mira.ziggurat_accepted: Carry water, or what passes for it in potions. The ziggurat has a Threshold Stone at its gate. Wake it before the climb.
dlg.mira.ziggurat_busy: The Sentinel still walks the rings of the ziggurat. The sun is long and the road is longer.
dlg.mira.ziggurat_thanks: The dunes are quiet and the caravans are crossing again. I will put your name in the ledger in gold.
dlg.mira.observatory_offer: The scholars of Lumeria, far to the south, have written in a panic: the old observatory has woken, and its Curator has decided that everything inside the walls is a specimen. They offer books in payment. I told them you prefer gold. Will you go?
dlg.mira.observatory_accepted: Take the scholars at their word, but not their maps. The observatory has a Threshold Stone at its south door.
dlg.mira.observatory_busy: The Curator is still cataloguing the observatory. Please do not become an entry.
dlg.mira.observatory_thanks: The lights of Lumeria are steady again. The scholars sent you a book, and a very polite letter. I kept the book.
dlg.mira.citadel_offer: The last letter is sealed with ash. Far to the east, in the Ashen Wastes, a citadel that burned a century ago has lit its forges once more, and a Colossus of cinder walks its courtyard. No one has come back from the road to tell me more. Will you go?
dlg.mira.citadel_accept: I will go to the Ashen Wastes.
dlg.mira.citadel_accepted: Bring everything you own that heals. The citadel has a Threshold Stone at its gate. Wake it, and then wake yourself.
dlg.mira.citadel_busy: The Colossus still burns in the citadel. The road east is hot and the ash is deep. Come back alive.
dlg.mira.citadel_thanks: The forges of the citadel are cold. Sit a moment; the road has not finished with you. There are four more letters, and they are all worse.
dlg.mira.forge_offer: A rider from Ironspine came in black with soot. Far to the north-east, under the old mine, the forge of the dwarves has relit, and something is hammering the mountain from the inside. The mountain does not like it. Will you go?
dlg.mira.forge_accept: I will go to the Deep Forge.
dlg.mira.forge_accepted: Take every potion you can carry. The forge has a Threshold Stone at its mouth, and you will want to wake it.
dlg.mira.forge_busy: The Tyrant is still at the anvil. Listen for the hammering; it will tell you where.
dlg.mira.forge_thanks: The hammering has stopped, and the mountain is quiet at last. I will tell Ironspine to thank you in iron.
dlg.mira.galleon_offer: A shipwright of Tidehaven writes that the galleon that sank in the bay a century ago has risen with the tide, crewed by what drowned in it. A Captain gives orders from the quarterdeck. Far south-west. Will you board her?
dlg.mira.galleon_accept: I will go to the galleon.
dlg.mira.galleon_accepted: Wake the stone on the beach before you go aboard. The tide here turns faster than you think.
dlg.mira.galleon_busy: The Captain still gives orders. The tide is on his side; be on yours.
dlg.mira.galleon_thanks: The galleon has gone back under, and the bay is flat. Tidehaven will sing your name at the next regatta.
dlg.mira.keep_offer: A runner from Frostveil collapsed at my door. The ice, he said, has grown a castle, far to the north, and a Sovereign sits in it who does not allow thaws. He could say no more, and I could not bring him round. Will you?
dlg.mira.keep_accept: I will go to the Glacier Keep.
dlg.mira.keep_accepted: Dress for a king's winter. The keep has a Threshold Stone at its gate; wake it before the cold wakes you.
dlg.mira.keep_busy: The Sovereign is still on his throne of ice. Come back before your fingers do not.
dlg.mira.keep_thanks: The ice is cracking and the rivers are running. Frostveil is thawing. Someone should tell them it is not a flood.
dlg.mira.vault_offer: The last letter is not a letter: it is a slab of black glass, cold to the touch, that arrived on my desk by itself. It points east, into the ash. Beneath the wastes there is a vault that was never meant to be opened. Will you go?
dlg.mira.vault_accept: I will go to the Obsidian Vault.
dlg.mira.vault_accepted: Take everything. The vault has a Threshold Stone at its door; wake it, and do not look at your reflection in the walls.
dlg.mira.vault_busy: The Warden still keeps the vault. The glass on my desk is humming.
dlg.mira.vault_thanks: The glass is quiet. You have cleared every dungeon the guild has a name for. I am not sure what to write on the ledger. 'Done', perhaps. Just that.
dlg.way.tamsin.q1_offer: I keep the road ledger here, and every week the slimes chew a page. Clear a few from the camp, and bring me some gel: it makes a fine binding glue.
dlg.way.tamsin.q1_thanks: That is a camp a person can sleep in. Thank you.
dlg.way.tamsin.q2_offer: My old friend Dorn keeps the Waystation at Ironspine. I have a letter for him that no rider will carry that far. You have the legs, and the stones. Will you?
dlg.way.tamsin.q2_thanks: He wrote back already, I see. Dorn always did answer fast. Good, good.
dlg.way.tamsin.q3_offer: The last page of my ledger is the longest: tawny wolves, worse every year. Bring me a dozen of them, and their pelts, and I will close the book on them.
dlg.way.tamsin.q3_thanks: The ledger is closed. The roads of Verdalis are safe, and it is your doing. This was my father's cloak; it should be worn on the road.
dlg.way.tamsin.busy: The ledger can wait. The road cannot, so be careful.
dlg.way.tamsin.incoming: A letter from Elowen of the Whisperwood, at last! She says the forest is quiet. I do not believe her, but I like that she writes.
dlg.way.elowen.q1_offer: I light the lamps at Hollow's Edge so the dark knows where we are. The wisps run low. Hunt a few shade wolves and bring me what they shed.
dlg.way.elowen.q1_thanks: The lamps burn clean again. The forest approves, I think.
dlg.way.elowen.q2_offer: Tamsin keeps a road ledger at the Crossroads Camp, far from here. I owe her an answer, and the forest does not like letters. Would you carry it?
dlg.way.elowen.q2_thanks: She read it twice, you say? That is Tamsin. Thank you.
dlg.way.elowen.q3_offer: Something is hushing the forest paths, slimes of moss as thick as carpets. Clear them, and bring me their moss for the lamp-wicks.
dlg.way.elowen.q3_thanks: I can hear the birds again. Take the hook; I lit a thousand lamps with it, and it never once went out.
dlg.way.elowen.busy: The lamps are patient. Take care of yourself first.
dlg.way.elowen.incoming: A letter from Ilvi of Frostveil? She writes in ink that has frozen into the page. It will thaw, I hope, before I can read it.
dlg.way.dorn.q1_offer: Waystation stalls are slate-floored. The slate slimes have gnawed the floor. Kill some. Bring shards to patch.
dlg.way.dorn.q1_thanks: Floors are flat. Horses are calm. Good.
dlg.way.dorn.q2_offer: Kessa keeps Ember Watch, east in the ash. Owes me for a horse. Take her this letter. She will pretend not to care.
dlg.way.dorn.q3_offer: Rust slimes are eating the pass rails. Twelve of them. Eight flakes of rust, for the smith to study. Then the rails hold.
dlg.way.dorn.q3_thanks: Rails hold. Take the goad. Horses will do anything for it, and so will cart-drivers.
dlg.way.dorn.incoming: Letter from Tamsin? She still writes small. Always did.
dlg.way.zahra.q1_offer: My water skins leak, and the sand slimes are the reason: they chew the stitches. Drive off a few, and bring me gel to seal the seams.
dlg.way.zahra.q1_thanks: Not a drop lost! You will do very well in the desert, my friend.
dlg.way.zahra.q2_offer: A scholar named Ottavio is writing a book about caravans, and has the cheek to ask for my route. I will give it, in a letter. Would you take it to Lantern Rest?
dlg.way.zahra.q2_thanks: He has already sent me three pages of questions. Typical! Thank you, truly.
dlg.way.zahra.q3_offer: The dune wolves have grown bold: they follow caravans for days. Twelve of them, and eight pelts for the cold nights. Then the road is ours again.
dlg.way.zahra.q3_thanks: The road is ours, and the caravans will sing about it. Take this mantle; the desert is cold at night, and you will want it.
dlg.way.zahra.busy: Take your time, friend. The desert has all the time there is.
dlg.way.zahra.incoming: A letter from Kessa of the Ember Watch? Fire and dust, that woman. Read it aloud, someone, I want to hear her bad temper.
dlg.way.ilvi.q1_offer: I fish through the ice, and the cold store keeps the catch. The ice slimes crack the lining. Drive off a few. Bring crystals.
dlg.way.ilvi.q1_thanks: The store holds. The fish will last the winter.
dlg.way.ilvi.q2_offer: A lamplighter in the Whisperwood, far south-west, once sent me a lamp. I never thanked her. This letter will. Will you carry it?
dlg.way.ilvi.q2_thanks: She answered. Warm words. I will keep them by the stove.
dlg.way.ilvi.q3_offer: White wolves circle the hut at night. Twelve of them, and eight tufts of fur. Then I can sleep.
dlg.way.ilvi.q3_thanks: I can sleep. The hut is safe. Take the spear; it has pulled a thousand fish out of the dark.
dlg.way.ilvi.busy: The ice is patient. So am I.
dlg.way.ilvi.incoming: From Marlo of Tidehaven? A sailor writing to an ice-fisher. We must be the only two people who understand each other.
dlg.way.marlo.q1_offer: I keep the Brinewatch lantern for the ships that no longer come. The tide slimes foul the lens. Clear a few, friend, and bring pearls to polish it.
dlg.way.marlo.q1_thanks: Bright as a morning. The ships will find us, if any ever do.
dlg.way.marlo.q2_offer: There is an ice-fisher at Rimewatch, far north, who writes to me at the turn of each season. I am late. Carry her my answer, and a bad joke.
dlg.way.marlo.q2_thanks: She laughed? In the ice? Well, then I was not late at all.
dlg.way.marlo.q3_offer: The pearl slimes have crowded the shallows where my old ship went down. Twelve of them cleared, and eight handfuls of their dust, and the wreck is mine to mourn in peace.
dlg.way.marlo.q3_thanks: Peace at last. Take my coat, friend. It has known every storm of the coast, and it is warm.
dlg.way.marlo.busy: The tide will wait, friend. Mind your feet.
dlg.way.marlo.incoming: A letter from Lin of Lumeria? A scholar of the stars writing to an old sailor. Well, the stars never failed me.
dlg.way.kessa.q1_offer: The beacon needs fuel. Ember slimes carry cores. Kill six, bring me four more than that.
dlg.way.kessa.q1_thanks: The beacon burns. You are useful. That is rare.
dlg.way.kessa.q2_offer: Zahra at the caravanserai still owes me for a horse. Tell her I know. Take the letter. Do not read it.
dlg.way.kessa.q2_thanks: She paid? ...Fine. Good. Do not tell anyone I said good.
dlg.way.kessa.q3_offer: The char slimes are nesting in the old furnaces. Twelve. Eight chunks, for the beacon. Then the Watch can rest a night.
dlg.way.kessa.q3_thanks: The Watch rests. Take the plate; it was my mother's. Do not scratch it.
dlg.way.kessa.busy: Unfinished. The ash waits for no one.
dlg.way.kessa.incoming: Dorn. Of course it is Dorn. Hand me that.
dlg.way.ottavio.q1_offer: I am cataloguing the glow of Lumeria and the instruments need star dust. Cull some slimes, dear traveler, and bring me samples. Do mind the margins.
dlg.way.ottavio.q1_thanks: Splendid samples! Properly dry. I shall cite you in the footnotes.
dlg.way.ottavio.q2_offer: An old captain at Brinewatch Post knows more about the stars than anyone at the Archive, and I have not told him so. This letter does. Would you be so kind?
dlg.way.ottavio.q2_thanks: He replied with a single line, which is rather better than most of my colleagues manage. Thank you.
dlg.way.ottavio.q3_offer: The nebula slimes are the final piece of my study. Twelve of them, I regret to say, and eight measures of their ash. The result will change what we know of the sky.
dlg.way.ottavio.q3_thanks: Magnificent! The sky is changed, and so am I. Please keep this greatcoat; my travels are done, and yours are only beginning.
dlg.way.ottavio.busy: The data will keep. You will not, if you rush.
dlg.way.ottavio.incoming: From Zahra of the Caravanserai? She writes the way she haggles: briefly, and with a surprising number of numbers. I am delighted.
dlg.mira.ring: Eight letters went round the world, and every one came back. Tamsin, Elowen, Dorn, Zahra, Ilvi, Marlo, Kessa, Ottavio: they all write to me now, and they all say the same thing. Someone walked the ring. The guild has a mantle for that, sewn from the road dust of every outpost.
dlg.mira.ring_thanks: Wear it where the road is long. And if you meet a stranger at an outpost fire, tell them the ring is closed. They will know what you mean.
speaker.tutor_pip: Pip, a lad of the village
dlg.pip.hello: Oh! A traveler from far away, Mira says. I am Pip. I know the meadows better than the slimes do. Ask me anything.
dlg.pip.q.heal: How do I get better when I am hurt?
dlg.pip.q.map: How do I not get lost?
dlg.pip.a.fight: Walk up to a slime and hit it: J or Space, or the attack button if you are on a phone. Slimes are slow, wolves are not. Fight the green ones first, then the grey. Watch your health, and eat bread when it is low (open the bag with I).
dlg.pip.a.heal: Bread and potions in the bag, but the best cure is a Threshold Stone: touch one and you are whole again. Every village has one in its square, and there is one at an inn bed too, if you have the coins.
dlg.pip.a.money: The guild clerk in a town gives work every day: hunt a few creatures, bring back what they drop. Elders and innkeepers have jobs too, and the shops buy what you find (the Sell tab).
dlg.pip.a.stones: Wake one by touching it, and you can come back to it from any other stone you have woken: pick a place from the list, and you are there. Wake every one you pass. Mira says the long roads are made of them.
dlg.pip.a.first: Talk to Mira, in the square. She has letters from the far dungeons, but start with the slimes in the meadow, and the barrow to the north-west, and the cellar to the north-east. Then the outposts, with the wayfarers; they all have stories.
dlg.pip.a.map: M opens the map of what you have seen: zoom with + and -, move it with W A S D or by dragging, and C brings you back to yourself. Villages are yellow, dungeons violet. The regions have names at the top of the screen, and every outpost has a signpost. When you are really lost, find a stone, or a village. There is always one, somewhere.
ui.protagonist_hint_touch: Tap a name to see it, tap it again to choose it
dlg.pip.story.ren.ask: I keep seeing numbers. Is that normal?
dlg.pip.story.ren.o1: Numbers? Over the slimes? Ha. Well, my mother says the meadow is a mess and the roof leaks. Six slimes and four gel, and you will see if your numbers are any good.
dlg.pip.story.ren.busy1: Six green slimes and four slime gel. The numbers will tell you where they are, I suppose.
dlg.pip.story.ren.o2: Your numbers were good! Now the sheep: four tawny wolves are after them, and I need three furs for blankets.
dlg.pip.story.ren.busy2: Four tawny wolves, three furs. Mind the claws: your numbers will not mention those.
dlg.pip.story.ren.done: You are the first person who found the world in order. Take it as a compliment. And keep the blade: it is yours now.
dlg.pip.story.sakura.ask: Do you know anything about mana?
dlg.pip.story.sakura.o1: Mana? You are the one who lights up when you walk! The herbalist says mint and spore caps hold a little. Four leaves, three caps, and you can test whatever you like.
dlg.pip.story.sakura.busy1: Four mint leaves, three spore caps. Not the ones that are still attached to the myconid, please.
dlg.pip.story.sakura.o2: Nothing exploded? Good. Now a proper test: eight green slimes. If your equation is right, they will not even notice.
dlg.pip.story.sakura.busy2: Eight green slimes. Stand back a little, and aim a little to the left, I hear it helps.
dlg.pip.story.sakura.done: The data is in, Doctor Mori. The meadow thanks you and so do I. Take the staff: it points where you point it. Usually.
dlg.pip.story.daichi.ask: Is there anyone here who needs help?
dlg.pip.story.daichi.o1: Help? Everyone! Five tawny wolves have been circling the pens for three nights. If you could drive them off...
dlg.pip.story.daichi.busy1: Five tawny wolves, by the pens. Take your time. And your shield.
dlg.pip.story.daichi.o2: The pens are quiet. Now the roofs: six slime gel to patch them, and three mint slimes out of the lanes.
dlg.pip.story.daichi.busy2: Six gel and three mint slimes. The roofs will hold, you will see.
dlg.pip.story.daichi.done: Everybody is out of trouble, because of you. The village wants you to have this axe. It is heavy, but you know how to carry things.
dlg.pip.story.haruka.ask: Are there animals around here that need care?
dlg.pip.story.haruka.o1: Animals? Plenty, and a few cuts. Mint leaves are good for poultices, and a couple of tawny furs for bandaging the little ones. Five leaves, two furs.
dlg.pip.story.haruka.busy1: Five mint leaves, two tawny furs. The poultice does not make itself, you know.
dlg.pip.story.haruka.o2: The animals sleep better already. But three myconids and four green slimes keep frightening them. Calmly, but firmly.
dlg.pip.story.haruka.busy2: Three myconids, four slimes. And do not worry about them: they get over it.
dlg.pip.story.haruka.done: Even the slimes are quiet. I think they like you. Take the cane: the herbalist made it for someone who listens.
dlg.pip.story.marco.ask: Is there any way to cook something in this village?
dlg.pip.story.marco.o1: Cook? My mother cooks, and she says no one has ever added slime gel to a sauce. Three gel and four mint leaves, if you want to be the first.
dlg.pip.story.marco.busy1: Three slime gel, four mint leaves. And please, do not tell my mother what it is for.
dlg.pip.story.marco.o2: My mother tasted it and she is still talking about it. Now the valve you want to try: five green slimes and two myconids, out where nobody lives.
dlg.pip.story.marco.busy2: Five slimes, two myconids. Stand a bit away from whatever you are making, I would.
dlg.pip.story.marco.done: The whole village smelled it and we all liked it. Take the cleaver: it is for someone who knows what to do with a kitchen.
dlg.pip.story.yuki.ask: Is there anything here worth stealing?
dlg.pip.story.yuki.o1: Steal? Here? Nobody locks anything. But the herbalist needs mint, three leaves, and some tawny wolves are scaring her off. You could be useful in the dark.
dlg.pip.story.yuki.busy1: Three mint leaves, three tawny wolves. Not a word to anyone about how you got them.
dlg.pip.story.yuki.o2: The herbalist is happy and she does not know why. Now the lane to the east: five mint slimes and two myconids block it. A quiet exit, if you like.
dlg.pip.story.yuki.busy2: Five mint slimes, two myconids. Quiet, remember.
dlg.pip.story.yuki.done: The lane is open and nobody saw anything. Take the dagger: it was left to someone who knows what to do with it.
dlg.pip.story.lena.ask: Is there a doctor in the village?
dlg.pip.story.lena.o1: A doctor? There is the herbalist, who is very old. She says a doctor measures things: four spore caps and two mint leaves, if you want to measure them.
dlg.pip.story.lena.busy1: Four spore caps, two mint leaves. Gently, they are still alive.
dlg.pip.story.lena.o2: She says you wrote down everything, even her cough. Now the myconids and the mint slimes: she wants to know what kills them.
dlg.pip.story.lena.busy2: Three myconids, three mint slimes. And the notes, do not forget the notes.
dlg.pip.story.lena.done: Everyone sleeps better knowing you are here. Take the blade: the herbalist says it was made for someone who looks at things for a long time.
dlg.pip.story.gideon.ask: Does anyone here know who I am?
dlg.pip.story.gideon.o1: Who you are? A tall man with a black sword, and the slimes follow you. Six of them, since this morning. If you could, uh, ask them to stop.
dlg.pip.story.gideon.busy1: Six green slimes. They really do follow you, you know.
dlg.pip.story.gideon.o2: The village wants to thank you with a tribute, the only one it knows. Four tawny wolves and two furs for the winter, if it is not too much to ask a king.
dlg.pip.story.gideon.busy2: Four tawny wolves, two furs. We call that a tribute, here. It is not like in the old days.
dlg.town.bran.after: Fenwick sleeps well since you came, Guest. Sit by the well whenever you like.
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_gardens.offer: Welcome to Fenwick, Guest. Lyra sends us one of you every few years, and every time the slimes notice first. They are in the cabbages again. Would you?
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_gardens.busy: Six of them, the green ones. They pop. Do not stand too close.
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_gardens.thanks: That was quick. It took the last Guest a week and a ladder. Take some bread.
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_wolves.offer: The carts to Aldermere have not left in a month. Wolves, to the east, on the road. For you it is a morning walk, I suspect.
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_wolves.busy: Five wolves and two furs. The tanner will do the rest.
dlg.town.bran.fenwick_wolves.thanks: The carts leave tomorrow. The tanner made you this. It fits everyone, he says, which worries me.
dlg.town.odile.after: The oven is warm and the door is open. That is all a village needs.
dlg.town.odile.fenwick_cakes.offer: You have the look of someone who has not eaten since another world. I can fix that, if you bring me berries. The bushes are full; shake them.
dlg.town.odile.fenwick_cakes.busy: Six handfuls of berries and two herbs. Do not eat them on the way. Everyone does.
dlg.town.odile.fenwick_cakes.thanks: Four cakes for you, and the smell for the whole street.
dlg.town.tobin.after: When I grow up I am going to be a Guest. Bran says it does not work like that. Bran is old.
dlg.town.tobin.fenwick_letter.offer: Are you the Guest? Really? Can you take a letter to the guild in Aldermere? It says I want to join. I am nine. I wrote that I am twelve.
dlg.town.tobin.fenwick_letter.busy: Aldermere is east, a little north, past the wolves. Give it to the quartermaster. He has a beard like a broom.
dlg.town.tobin.fenwick_letter.thanks: He read it? He READ it? What did the beard do?
dlg.town.hestia.after: The board is yours, Guest. Leave something for the others; they need the practice.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_trial.offer: So you are the one Mira wrote about. This is the mother guild; every rank in the world begins at this desk. The trial is the same for all. Most take three days.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_trial.busy: Six mint slimes, four myconids. Take your time. Nobody does, of your kind.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_trial.thanks: Before lunch. Of course. I will stop being surprised by Guests one of these years.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_crown.offer: There is a slime with a crown in a cellar west of here, not far from Fenwick. Three parties tried. All three came back sticky. I would like a fourth opinion.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_crown.busy: The Gel King. You will know it by the crown, and by the size.
dlg.town.hestia.aldermere_crown.thanks: One blow, the scouts said. One. Take this sword; it was meant for whoever managed it, and I had given up hope of handing it over.
dlg.town.rook.after: Stores are full. First time since I took the job. Do not tell the guildmaster, she will find a use for them.
dlg.town.rook.aldermere_stores.offer: A letter? From Fenwick? ...Nine years old, by the handwriting. I will keep it. Since you are here and have two arms: I am short of ore and of wood.
dlg.town.rook.aldermere_stores.busy: Four of ore, six logs. Rocks and trees. They do not fight back, mostly.
dlg.town.rook.aldermere_stores.thanks: Counted twice. All there. Take a pike from the rack; it is the one thing I have too many of.
dlg.town.selwyn.after: I have started a new shelf. It is labelled 'Things the Guest did'. It is already full.
dlg.town.selwyn.aldermere_samples.offer: A Guest! Do not move. No, do move, I need samples. Gel, five jars' worth, and three spore caps. For the bestiary. You keep one too, I am told, in your head.
dlg.town.selwyn.aldermere_samples.busy: Five of gel, three caps. Label them if you can. Nobody ever labels them.
dlg.town.selwyn.aldermere_samples.thanks: Unlabelled. Perfect anyway. Have these; I mix them myself and only one in ten explodes.
speaker.shrine_keeper_maren: Sister Maren, keeper of Lyra's shrine
dlg.maren.hello: Lyra's shrine is small, Guest, and so am I. But she talks to me sometimes, and lately she talks about you.
dlg.maren.ren.ask: The numbers I see: some of them are wrong.
dlg.maren.ren.done: A whole office, under a mountain, and you closed it. Lyra says you may keep the stapler. I do not know what she means and I am afraid to ask.
dlg.maren.ren.q1.offer: Wrong how? ...A second line, under the first, in a hand you know. Oh dear. Go and look at more of them. Eight should do.
dlg.maren.ren.q1.busy: Eight green slimes. Read the second line, not the first.
dlg.maren.ren.q1.thanks: The same four digits on every one. An extension number, you say? I do not know what that is, and I do not like it.
dlg.maren.ren.q2.offer: There is an ink that shows what the Threshold hides. It needs spore caps and mint. The myconids and the mint slimes will not give them up politely.
dlg.maren.ren.q2.busy: Four caps, four leaves. I will warm the bowl.
dlg.maren.ren.q2.thanks: There. The line points north-west, to the old barrow. Something there is counting too.
dlg.maren.ren.q3.offer: The warden of Grunmoor has stood a thousand years and never counted anything. Now it does. Go and see what it has of yours.
dlg.maren.ren.q3.busy: Grunmoor Barrow, north-west of Fenwick. Mind the warden; or rather, let it mind you.
dlg.maren.ren.q3.thanks: It fell, and the numbers stopped. Take these: the guild keeps them for whoever ends a thing like that.
dlg.maren.sakura.ask: My machine. I think it is still running.
dlg.maren.sakura.done: You gave a lecture to a star-curator and it took notes. Lyra asks for a copy. So do I, though I will not understand a word.
dlg.maren.sakura.q1.offer: Running? Child, the mint slimes have been glowing since the night you fell. Glowing in equations. Go and see.
dlg.maren.sakura.q1.busy: Eight mint slimes, three leaves. Try not to correct their mathematics.
dlg.maren.sakura.q1.thanks: Your handwriting, on a leaf. Lyra finds this very funny. I find it worrying.
dlg.maren.sakura.q2.offer: You want to build an instrument. Of course you do. Gel for the lens, resin to hold it. The pines have resin if you ask the trunk firmly.
dlg.maren.sakura.q2.busy: Five of gel, two of resin. I will find you a table.
dlg.maren.sakura.q2.thanks: It works. It points south, at Mint Hollow. And it hums your name.
dlg.maren.sakura.q3.offer: The Matron of the Hollow has swallowed a piece of your machine and grown clever. A clever slime is the last thing Verdalis needs.
dlg.maren.sakura.q3.busy: Mint Hollow, south-west of Fenwick. It will try to argue. Do not let it.
dlg.maren.sakura.q3.thanks: Gone, and the glow with it. This robe was woven for a scholar. You are the nearest thing we have.
dlg.maren.daichi.ask: I smell smoke. Nobody else does.
dlg.maren.daichi.done: They have named the citadel's well after you. You will say it was nothing. Say it to the forty people who walked out of there.
dlg.maren.daichi.q1.offer: Smoke. Yes. The wolves smell it too: they are running toward the road, toward the carts. First the people, you would say.
dlg.maren.daichi.q1.busy: Six tawny wolves, before they reach the carts.
dlg.maren.daichi.q1.thanks: The road is safe. And their fur was singed. Something is burning that does not burn here.
dlg.maren.daichi.q2.offer: A firebreak, you call it. Timber and stone in a ring, before there is any fire to stop. Nobody here thinks that way. Do it.
dlg.maren.daichi.q2.busy: Six logs, four stones. The trees and the rocks will not mind.
dlg.maren.daichi.q2.thanks: The ring is laid. And the smoke comes from one place now: the old barrow.
dlg.maren.daichi.q3.offer: The warden of Grunmoor is burning and does not fall. That is your fire, Guest. I think you know how it ends.
dlg.maren.daichi.q3.busy: Grunmoor Barrow, north-west of Fenwick. Go in. You always do.
dlg.maren.daichi.q3.thanks: Out. Cold. The smith made this axe for a hand that does not shake. Yours does not.
dlg.maren.haruka.ask: The slimes here are sick, Sister.
dlg.maren.haruka.done: The wolves of Whisperwood sleep at the edge of the camp now. The children name them. Lyra's cat, I am told, is jealous.
dlg.maren.haruka.q1.offer: Sick? Slimes? ...You touched one. Of course you did. Bring me samples, then, and calm the worst of them.
dlg.maren.haruka.q1.busy: Eight green slimes, four of gel. Wash your hands. I do not know why I said that.
dlg.maren.haruka.q1.thanks: The gel is warm. Slime gel is never warm. You were right, and I owe you an apology and a kettle.
dlg.maren.haruka.q2.offer: A medicine for monsters. The guild will laugh. Let them. Herbs and berries, from the bushes; I will lend you the shrine's pot.
dlg.maren.haruka.q2.busy: Five herbs, six handfuls of berries.
dlg.maren.haruka.q2.thanks: They drank it. All of them, in a line, like children. But one did not come: the big one, in the Hollow.
dlg.maren.haruka.q3.offer: The Matron is the mother of every mint slime in Verdalis, and she is past any tonic. You know what a vet does then. I am sorry.
dlg.maren.haruka.q3.busy: Mint Hollow, south-west of Fenwick. Be quick. Be kind.
dlg.maren.haruka.q3.thanks: It is done, and the meadow is quiet. This robe keeps harm away. Lyra says you have taken enough of it for others.
dlg.maren.marco.ask: Something here is under pressure. I can hear it.
dlg.maren.marco.done: A ship raised, a crew fed, a captain retired. The harbour wants to make you mayor. I told them you would rather have the kitchen.
dlg.maren.marco.q1.offer: Pressure. The mushroom folk have been popping like corks all week. If that is your doing, it is also your job.
dlg.maren.marco.q1.busy: Six myconids, three caps. Stand upwind.
dlg.maren.marco.q1.thanks: Steam inside a mushroom. You say that with such delight. Please stop saying it with such delight.
dlg.maren.marco.q2.offer: A valve. I will pretend to know the word. Iron and wood, you say; the rocks and the trees have both.
dlg.maren.marco.q2.busy: Four of ore, four logs. The smith is curious. Do not explain it to him yet.
dlg.maren.marco.q2.thanks: It whistles. And the whistle comes loudest from the cellar by Fenwick, where the big one lives.
dlg.maren.marco.q3.offer: The Gel King is three times his size and still growing. You know what a sealed pot does. So does half of your old kitchen.
dlg.maren.marco.q3.busy: Mossveil Cellar, north of Fenwick. Open him gently.
dlg.maren.marco.q3.thanks: No explosion. I am almost disappointed. The smith sends this, and asks what a 'gasket' is.
dlg.maren.yuki.ask: Someone has been in my pocket. That is not possible.
dlg.maren.yuki.done: You walked into a tomb full of gold and came out with one painting, yours, and hung it beside the first. The Sentinel would have let you take everything. Lyra wept.
dlg.maren.yuki.q1.offer: Your pocket that nobody can open? Then you will like this: half the town has lost a spoon, and the wolves are wearing them.
dlg.maren.yuki.q1.busy: Six tawny wolves, two furs. Count the spoons.
dlg.maren.yuki.q1.thanks: Eleven spoons and a candlestick. And a corner of canvas, painted. You have gone quite pale.
dlg.maren.yuki.q2.offer: You want to catch a thief. I will not ask how you know the way. Resin and dry branches, you say. The pines and the dead trees.
dlg.maren.yuki.q2.thanks: Sticky footprints, as big as a table, going north-west. Into the barrow. Nothing alive has feet like that.
dlg.maren.yuki.q3.offer: The warden collects what does not belong here. Your painting does not. Neither, forgive me, do you. Go and settle which of you keeps it.
dlg.maren.yuki.q3.busy: Grunmoor Barrow, north-west of Fenwick. Steal it back. Just this once I will call it that.
dlg.maren.yuki.q3.thanks: You hung it in the shrine. It is the first beautiful thing these walls have had. Take this; the guild pays honest work honestly.
dlg.maren.lena.ask: I have seen this death before. On my table.
dlg.maren.lena.done: You signed a death certificate for a man a thousand years late, and he thanked you. I have kept the shrine thirty years and never seen Lyra so quiet.
dlg.maren.lena.q1.offer: Before? Then you will want to see more. The mushroom folk lie down and do not get up. No mark on them. Bring me what you find.
dlg.maren.lena.q1.busy: Six myconids, four caps. You are humming. Please do not hum.
dlg.maren.lena.q1.thanks: The same grey ring under every cap. You drew it in your notes before I showed you. That frightens me more than the ring.
dlg.maren.lena.q2.offer: A test. With leaves. I thought you only looked at the dead. Very well: mint and herbs.
dlg.maren.lena.q2.busy: Four leaves of mint, four herbs.
dlg.maren.lena.q2.thanks: It turned black. You say that means it came from the water, and the water comes from the cellar. I believe you. Nobody argues with you twice.
dlg.maren.lena.q3.offer: The Gel King swallowed something that fell with you: the last thing you were studying. It is killing the meadow from below.
dlg.maren.lena.q3.busy: Mossveil Cellar, north of Fenwick. Write it up afterwards. You will anyway.
dlg.maren.lena.q3.thanks: Case closed, you say, and you almost smiled. Take the blade and the robe. A doctor of the dead should at least be warm.
dlg.maren.gideon.ask: Something in this land still calls me king.
dlg.maren.gideon.done: You went home, and you burned the throne room, and then you helped them build a granary where it stood. Lyra says she misjudged you. She has never said that about anyone.
dlg.maren.gideon.q1.offer: King. Yes. The wolves have been stealing sheep 'for the throne', the shepherds say. Which throne, I wonder. Deal with your court.
dlg.maren.gideon.q1.busy: Eight tawny wolves. Dismiss them. Permanently.
dlg.maren.gideon.q1.thanks: The shepherds sent a cheese. For you. Nobody ever sent you a cheese before, did they?
dlg.maren.gideon.q2.offer: You wish to repay them. From your own hand. I will sit down; I am not as young as I was. Furs and gel will mend what was lost.
dlg.maren.gideon.q2.thanks: They bowed to you. Not from fear. You did not know what to do with your hands. It was the best thing I have seen all year.
dlg.maren.gideon.q3.offer: There is a king in the cellar by Fenwick. He found a crown that fell with you, and he says it is yours if you come and rule. Well?
dlg.maren.gideon.q3.busy: Mossveil Cellar, north of Fenwick. Give him your answer.
dlg.maren.gideon.q3.thanks: You left the crown in the mud. Take this blade instead. It suits a man who has decided what he is.
dlg.maren.ren.interlude: The warden's number was your old desk, was it not? Lyra says the Threshold let it through with you. There will be more. You will count them.
dlg.maren.ren.q4.offer: Word from Ironspine, north-east, past the hills: the slimes in the mine have begun to queue. To queue, Guest. With numbered tickets. That is yours, is it not?
dlg.maren.ren.q4.busy: Eight slate slimes, four shards, in Ironspine. Wake a Threshold Stone there; it is a long walk twice.
dlg.maren.ren.q4.thanks: Numbers scratched on every shard. A timetable. Somebody is running that mine the way your old world ran you.
dlg.maren.ren.q5.offer: I want to read their books. They keep them on rust, the rust slimes carry it, and the ore is the ink. Do not laugh; you worked somewhere very like it.
dlg.maren.ren.q5.busy: Four rust flakes, five of ore.
dlg.maren.ren.q5.thanks: Every line ends in the same name: the Foreman. He has not let anyone leave in forty years.
dlg.maren.ren.q6.offer: The Foreman of Ironspine Mine has your old manager's voice, the miners say, though they never met him. You know what to tell him.
dlg.maren.ren.q6.busy: Ironspine Mine. He will ask whether it can wait until Monday.
dlg.maren.ren.q6.thanks: The miners went home. All of them, at once, at five o'clock. Take these, and take a day off. That is an order from a goddess.
dlg.maren.sakura.interlude: So the door you opened never quite closed. Lyra is not angry. She says: next time, a smaller door.
dlg.maren.sakura.q4.offer: The sky over Lumeria, south of everything, has a new constellation. It is shaped like a diagram. Your diagram. The slimes there are copying it.
dlg.maren.sakura.q4.busy: Eight glow slimes, four of star dust, in Lumeria. Wake a Stone when you get there.
dlg.maren.sakura.q4.thanks: The dust arranges itself on the table. Into your thesis. Chapter three has a mistake, it seems, and the dust has fixed it.
dlg.maren.sakura.q5.offer: Someone is reading you, child, and writing in the margins. I can find who, with ash from the nebula slimes and embers from the wisps.
dlg.maren.sakura.q5.busy: Three of nebula ash, three embers.
dlg.maren.sakura.q5.thanks: The smoke drew an eye, and a tower: the Starfall Observatory. Its curator has your machine's other half.
dlg.maren.sakura.q6.offer: The Curator will open your door again, a bigger one, to see what is on the other side. It is very polite about it. Stop it anyway.
dlg.maren.sakura.q6.busy: The Starfall Observatory, in Lumeria. It will have questions. Answer the first three.
dlg.maren.sakura.q6.thanks: A doctorate, then, examined by the stars. This staff was an archmage's. He would have hated your handwriting and loved your results.
dlg.maren.daichi.interlude: It was your fire, the one from the third floor. It followed you, and you put it out twice. Rest, if you know how.
dlg.maren.daichi.q4.offer: East, where the ground is ash: there are people there, at Ember Watch, and the fire has begun to walk toward them. I knew you would stand up before I finished.
dlg.maren.daichi.q4.busy: Eight ember slimes, four cores, in the Ashen Wastes. Wake the Stone at Ember Watch.
dlg.maren.daichi.q4.thanks: The cores are still hot in my hands, and they are all pulling the same way. Fire does not do that. Something calls it.
dlg.maren.daichi.q5.offer: You draw a map of where it is hottest and you go there. Every instinct I have says the opposite. Shards from the magma slimes, and stone.
dlg.maren.daichi.q5.thanks: The channel holds. And the heat has a heart: the Cinder Citadel. There are people still inside.
dlg.maren.daichi.q6.offer: The Colossus is the fire from your third floor, grown as tall as a tower. The floor will hold this time. I asked.
dlg.maren.daichi.q6.busy: The Cinder Citadel, in the Ashen Wastes. Count them on the way out.
dlg.maren.daichi.q6.thanks: Forty. All forty. The ash-wardens forged this plate for whoever did it, and never thought to make it in one man's size.
dlg.maren.haruka.interlude: You healed a thing nobody thought could be ill. Lyra asks whether you would look at her cat. I did not know she had a cat.
dlg.maren.haruka.q4.offer: A hunter came from Whisperwood, to the west. He said the shade wolves limp, all of them, on the same leg. I thought of you at once.
dlg.maren.haruka.q4.busy: Eight shade wolves, four shade wisps, in Whisperwood. There is a Stone at Hollow's Edge.
dlg.maren.haruka.q4.thanks: A thorn in every one. Not a thorn of this world: it is glass, and it smells of rain on a road.
dlg.maren.haruka.q5.offer: Glass from your road, in their paws. You cannot take it back, but you can ease it. Moss, from the moss slimes, and herbs.
dlg.maren.haruka.q5.thanks: They let you touch them. A whole pack. But the old one in the den will not come out, and the glass in him is as long as a sword.
dlg.maren.haruka.q6.offer: The Elder has guarded that wood since before the guild. He is in pain and he is very large. Be the vet he has never had.
dlg.maren.haruka.q6.busy: The Mossy Den, in Whisperwood. Speak softly. Then do what must be done.
dlg.maren.haruka.q6.thanks: The wood is quiet, and it is a kind quiet. The hunters stitched this cloak for you. They say it will keep you from being followed home. It will not.
dlg.maren.marco.interlude: You vented a king. The guild has no form for that. I have written 'cooking accident', which you will find familiar.
dlg.maren.marco.q4.offer: Tidehaven, on the south-west coast. The fishermen pull up crabs with handles. With handles, Guest, and a lid. Tell me that is not yours.
dlg.maren.marco.q4.busy: Eight shore crabs, four shells, in Tidehaven. Wake the Stone at Brinewatch.
dlg.maren.marco.q4.thanks: Stamped inside every shell: a maker's mark. You are blushing. It is your cookware.
dlg.maren.marco.q5.offer: You want to feed them to make them talk. It is the most sensible plan anyone has brought me this year. Pearls and coral, they trade in those.
dlg.maren.marco.q5.busy: Three tide pearls, three coral fragments.
dlg.maren.marco.q5.thanks: They talked through three helpings. A galleon went down the night you arrived, and its captain has been cooking ever since. Badly.
dlg.maren.marco.q6.offer: The Captain feeds his drowned crew from your pot, and the valve has rusted shut. When it goes, the harbour goes. You know the sound it makes first.
dlg.maren.marco.q6.busy: The Sunken Galleon, in Tidehaven. Do not taste anything.
dlg.maren.marco.q6.thanks: You opened the valve by hand and the whole bay smelled of dinner. The harbour sends mail of tide-scale, and forty recipes they want corrected.
dlg.maren.yuki.interlude: A thief robbed, and she gave the painting back. Lyra is telling everyone. I am sorry; she has few stories this good.
dlg.maren.yuki.q4.offer: A caravan from Sunscar, south-east, asked me whether the shrine had 'paintings from elsewhere' to sell. They had a list. Your second canvas was on it.
dlg.maren.yuki.q4.busy: Eight amber slimes, four amber drops, in Sunscar. The Stone is at the Dune Caravanserai.
dlg.maren.yuki.q4.thanks: There is a seal in the amber. A collector's seal. You know the type. You were the type.
dlg.maren.yuki.q5.offer: I will not ask what the stings are for. I will only observe that a shrine-keeper should not know the word 'grimaldello', and now I do.
dlg.maren.yuki.q5.busy: Three scorpion stings, three dune pelts.
dlg.maren.yuki.q5.thanks: The collector does not live in a house. He lives in the Sunken Ziggurat, and he has been dead for a thousand years.
dlg.maren.yuki.q6.offer: A whole tomb of stolen things, and one honest thief at the door. Take only what is yours. I should like to see whether you can.
dlg.maren.yuki.q6.busy: The Sunken Ziggurat, in Sunscar. Mind the floor. Mind everything.
dlg.maren.yuki.q6.thanks: One painting. I counted your pockets twice, forgive me. The caravans left you this blade in thanks: the roads are safe from a collector at last.
dlg.maren.lena.interlude: Your last case, finished in another world. You may close the file. Lyra kept the pen for you.
dlg.maren.lena.q4.offer: An ice-fisher wrote from Frostveil, in the north: she killed the same wolf on three mornings. She would like a second opinion. So would I.
dlg.maren.lena.q4.busy: Eight frost wolves, four pelts, in Frostveil. The Stone is at Rimewatch Hut.
dlg.maren.lena.q4.thanks: No rot. No warmth. And a tag on each, tied to the leg, in your hand: a number and a date that has not happened.
dlg.maren.lena.q5.offer: You can tell the hour of a death from ice? ...Of course you can. Crystals from the ice slimes, then, and owl feathers, for reasons I will not ask.
dlg.maren.lena.q5.busy: Four ice crystals, three owl feathers.
dlg.maren.lena.q5.thanks: The night you died. To the minute. And it began in the Frostveil Cavern, where a man has refused to lie down for a thousand years.
dlg.maren.lena.q6.offer: He caught the piece of your second chance that you did not use, and he has been using it on everyone. He is very tired. He needs a doctor who knows when to stop.
dlg.maren.lena.q6.thanks: He lay down, and so did all the others, and the snow covered them properly. Take this blade. It was a coroner's, in a city that is gone. It has been waiting for a steady hand.
dlg.maren.gideon.interlude: You refused a crown. Lyra did not think you would. She lost a wager to me, and I intend to collect.
dlg.maren.gideon.q4.offer: I have put this off. The Ashen Wastes, in the east. Your Wastes. They have a new master, and he rules in your name, and he is worse than you ever were.
dlg.maren.gideon.q4.busy: Eight char slimes, four char chunks, in the Ashen Wastes. The Stone is at Ember Watch. They may recognise you.
dlg.maren.gideon.q4.thanks: Your crest, burned into each one. You looked at it a long time. I did not think a face like yours could do that.
dlg.maren.gideon.q5.offer: The people of Ember Watch do not want your apology. They want a forge and warm houses. I find that I respect them enormously.
dlg.maren.gideon.q5.busy: Two golem cores, four ember cores.
dlg.maren.gideon.q5.thanks: They lit the forge with your own hands on the bellows, and an old woman called you 'lad'. And now they have told you where he sits: the Char Pit.
dlg.maren.gideon.q6.offer: He is what you were, with nothing to lose it for. He will offer you half. Then all of it. I am not worried. I only wanted to see your face when I said so.
dlg.maren.gideon.q6.busy: The Char Pit, in the Ashen Wastes. No speeches.
dlg.maren.gideon.q6.thanks: No speech. One blow. Then you asked where they kept the shovels. Wear the mantle, Gideon; it was a sovereign's, and for once it is on the right shoulders.
dlg.pip.story.gideon.done: The whole village agrees: you are a good king. Take the blade, it is nothing like the old one, but it suits you.
